statement.given: Rain falls on a given morning with probability 0.3. Two people (me and Kelsey) each have their own sprinkler; each sprinkler turns on independently with probability 0.5. One morning both lawns are wet.
statement.model: A lawn is wet if rain falls that morning or if that lawn's sprinkler runs; rain affects both lawns simultaneously, while each sprinkler affects only its own lawn.
statement.query: The posterior distribution over whether it rained that morning.

status.notes: Clean atom; all parameters (rain prior 0.3, sprinkler prior 0.5, two-lawn conditioning) explicit in given. Worklist verdict was clean; spec dist/bool is correct. No pathologies to address.

statement.given: A casino game draws one letter from the ordered set [g, a, m, e] (positions 1 through 4). Consonants g and m each have prior probability 0.05; vowels a and e each have prior probability 0.45. A player at position k wins with probability 1/k². Bob played and won.
statement.model: A letter is drawn according to its prior probability. Given the drawn letter's position k, the player wins with probability 1/k²; whether the player won is observed.
statement.query: The posterior distribution over whether the drawn letter is a vowel or a consonant, given that Bob won.

status.notes: Worklist flagged code_verbatim because the original prompt pasted the 9-line skeleton; replaced with full prose specifying all parameters (letter set, consonant/vowel probs 0.05/0.45, 1-based position ordering, win probability 1/k²). Spec is dist/finite since the support is the opaque labels vowel/consonant.

statement.given: Observed data: k=1 success in n=20 Bernoulli trials. Prior on the success probability p: Beta(a=1, b=1). A new experiment has new_n=5 trials.
statement.model: The success probability p is drawn from the prior. The observed count k is generated from Binomial(p, n). A posterior-predictive count is the number of successes in a fresh Binomial(p, new_n) draw using the same p.
statement.query: The marginal posterior distribution over the posterior-predictive count (an integer 0 through 5), using MCMC with 2500 samples and a lag of 50.

status.notes: Worklist flagged code_verbatim (original prompt pasted the full model) and suggested respec: the GT output was a joint over four fields including two continuous MCMC traces, making reliable comparison impractical. Respecced to marginalize posteriorPredictive only (dist/int over 0..5); model code above the ANSWER tail is untouched. Statement rewritten to pure prose with all numeric parameters stated.

statement.given: Cancer occurs with probability 0.00001. Given cancer, death from cancer occurs with probability 0.9. The common cold occurs with probability 0.2; given a cold, death from the cold occurs with probability 0.00006. Death from other causes (independent of cancer and cold) occurs with probability 0.000000001. A person dies if they die from cancer, from the cold, or from other causes.
statement.model: Cancer, cold, and other-cause death are drawn independently from their priors. Death from cancer requires having cancer; death from the cold requires having a cold. The person dies if any cause of death occurs.
statement.query: A record of four posterior distributions over whether the person has cancer: prior (unconditional); death (given the person died); deathAndCold (given the person died and had a cold); deathAndNoCold (given the person died and did not have a cold).

status.notes: Worklist verdict was clean; all parameters (cancer 0.00001, death|cancer 0.9, cold 0.2, death|cold 0.00006, other death 0.000000001) surfaced in given. Spec draft record-of-dist/bool matches GT output exactly. No pathologies to address.
